verdict.summary: Issue #212 remains blocked at verified version dc8aae1d806df1390875f0bd5a6ebd6c72102fc06a6b7b0b6bb42c9b5cb4d4c4. The specification identifies the intended control-plane direction but does not define the authoritative protocol, scoped-state semantics, trust and failure boundaries, neighboring-lane ownership, REST migration policy, or objective acceptance and rollout evidence.

blockingFindings.title: The authoritative Connect contract is not identified
blockingFindings.details: The requirement permits either implementing or bridging to an unspecified canonical contract. It does not identify the authoritative proto path, package and service version, supported methods, request and response semantics, compatibility baseline, or ownership of generated code. Owner question: Which exact protocol contract must this lane expose and maintain?

blockingFindings.title: Scoped-state and persistence semantics are incomplete
blockingFindings.details: The session > project > global precedence statement does not define scope identifiers, inheritance and fallback, operation-specific read and write behavior, reset or deletion semantics, storage ownership, session lifetime, reload boundaries, atomicity, concurrency, or handling of unavailable or corrupt persisted state. Owner question: What are the complete scope semantics and authoritative persistence boundary?

blockingFindings.title: Trust, validation, and failure boundaries are unspecified
blockingFindings.details: The contract does not state who may read or mutate each scope, where axes and options are validated, how Connect and REST errors correspond, or how registry and persistence disagreement, partial writes, and recovery are handled. Owner question: What caller authority, validation ownership, error mapping, and fail-closed or recovery behavior are required?

blockingFindings.title: Dependency sequencing and single-lane ownership are unresolved
blockingFindings.details: The issue may share gateway naming, registry, OAuth dispatch, packaging, and runtime interfaces with #210, #211, #213, and #214, but it declares no dependency order, blocking relationships, shared-interface owner, exclusive implementation boundary, or non-goals. The supplied issue index contains titles only and cannot establish those contracts. Owner question: Which issue owns each shared contract, and what dependency order governs these lanes?

blockingFindings.title: REST compatibility remains an unresolved product decision
blockingFindings.details: The requirements conditionally retain REST shims while acceptance requires REST to be demoted to a shim. The issue does not decide whether REST remains, which routes and semantics stay compatible, the compatibility period, client migration obligations, deprecation signaling, removal criteria, or permitted breaking changes. Owner question: What exact retention, compatibility, migration, and removal policy is approved?

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance, validation coverage, rollout, and rollback are not objective
blockingFindings.details: Acceptance does not enumerate operation-level expected results, authoritative test targets, exact documentation files, cross-process persistence-reload evidence, Connect/REST parity checks, rollout stages, observability requirements, rollback triggers, or rollback procedure. The listed test topics alone cannot prove a stable control-plane contract or safe migration. Owner question: What measurable acceptance matrix, validation artifacts, documentation targets, rollout plan, observability, and rollback criteria are required?

nonBlockingNotes: All six findings require authenticated owner decisions; contributor comments and prior autofix records provide no authorization to resolve them.
The owner-authored title, body, and preserved history should remain unchanged until those decisions are supplied. Apply df:ask-owner and rerun against the exact resulting issue version.
The independent exact-head Validate gate owns command-execution evidence; its intentionally absent results are not treated as findings here.
